title: Patofisiologi Stroke
subtitle: Kimi rerun: neuro_vascular
summary: Kuliah tentang patofisiologi stroke yang mencakup definisi, klasifikasi (iskemik vs hemoragik), faktor risiko (dapat dimodifikasi dan tidak dapat dimodifikasi), patofisiologi iskemia serebral (kaskade iskemik, eksitotoksisitas, konsep penumbra), neuroproteksi, prinsip manajemen akut, serta aspek nutrisi dalam perawatan stroke. Menyertakan kaskade iskemik dari oklusi pembuluh darah hingga kematian neuron dan konsep penumbra iskemik sebagai target intervensi akut.

sections.title: Definisi dan Klasifikasi Stroke

content.text: WHO definition: Rapidly developing clinical signs of focal (or global) disturbance of cerebral function, lasting more than 24 hours or leading to death, with no apparent cause other than of vascular origin. Stroke is classified into: ISCHEMIC STROKE (85% of all strokes) - from thrombosis, embolism, or systemic hypoperfusion; HEMORRHAGIC STROKE (15%) - intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) or subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). TRANSIENT ISCHEMIC ATTACK (TIA): focal neurological deficit resolving within 24 hours (traditional) or without tissue infarction on imaging (tissue-based definition).

sections.title: Faktor Risiko

content.text: NON-MODIFIABLE: Age (risk doubles each decade after 55), sex (men > women, but women have higher mortality), race (African Americans, Hispanics higher risk), family history, prior stroke/TIA. MODIFIABLE: Hypertension (most important modifiable risk factor), diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, smoking, dyslipidemia, obesity, physical inactivity, excessive alcohol, obstructive sleep apnea, metabolic syndrome. NUTRITIONAL RISK FACTORS: High sodium intake, low potassium intake, high saturated fat, low fruit/vegetable consumption, obesity (BMI >25).
Hypertension is the single most important modifiable risk factor for both ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke

sections.title: Kaskade Iskemik dan Konsep Penumbra

content.text: ISCHEMIC CASCADE: Within seconds of vessel occlusion, the ischemic cascade begins: (1) ENERGY FAILURE - cessation of oxidative phosphorylation, ATP depletion, ion pump dysfunction (Na+/K+-ATPase, Ca2+-ATPase); (2) MEMBRANE DEPOLARIZATION - influx of Na+, Cl-, H2O (cytotoxic edema), efflux of K+; (3) EXCITOTOXICITY - massive release of glutamate into synaptic cleft, overstimulation of NMDA and AMPA receptors, excessive Ca2+ influx; (4) CALCIUM OVERLOAD - activates lipases, proteases, nucleases, NO synthase, leading to free radical production; (5) FREE RADICAL FORMATION - reactive oxygen species (ROS) damage lipids, proteins, DNA; (6) INFLAMMATION - leukocyte infiltration, microglial activation, cytokine release, BBB disruption (vasogenic edema); (7) CELL DEATH - necrosis in the core, apoptosis in the penumbra. PENUMBRA CONCEPT: The ischemic penumbra is tissue surrounding the irreversibly damaged infarct core that is hemodynamically compromised but still viable. Cerebral blood flow (CBF) in the penumbra is approximately 10-20 mL/100g/min (normal 50-60). Penumbra tissue can be salvaged with prompt reperfusion. The goal of acute stroke therapy is to save the penumbra. Penumbra exists for a limited time window - typically 3-6 hours, extendable to 24 hours in selected cases with advanced imaging.
1. Gagal energi: deplesi ATP
2. Depolarisasi membran: edema sitotoksik
3. Eksitotoksisitas: pelepasan glutamat berlebihan
4. Overload kalsium: aktivasi enzim degradatif
5. Formasi radikal bebas: ROS
6. Inflamasi: infiltrasi leukosit
7. Kematian sel: nekrosis (inti), apoptosis (penumbra)
Penumbra = salvageable tissue around infarct core; the therapeutic target in acute stroke; time-sensitive

sections.title: Neuroproteksi dan Manajemen Akut

content.text: NEUROPROTECTION: Strategies to protect the ischemic penumbra. Despite many candidates in research, no neuroprotective agent has proven effective in clinical trials. Hypothermia shows promise. Maintaining physiological parameters (normoglycemia, normothermia, normotension) is essential. ACUTE MANAGEMENT: TIME IS BRAIN. IV thrombolysis with alteplase (tPA) within 4.5 hours of symptom onset (inclusion: age >=18, measurable deficit, CT excludes hemorrhage; exclusion: recent surgery, active bleeding, INR>1.7, platelets<100k, prior ICH, severe stroke NIHSS>25). Mechanical thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion (ICA, proximal MCA) up to 24 hours in selected patients (DAWN, DEFUSE 3 trials). Blood pressure management: permissive hypertension in ischemic stroke (up to 220/120) unless thrombolysis candidate (lower to <185/110). Supportive care: airway, oxygenation, hydration, temperature control, glycemic control.
'Time is brain' - every minute of large vessel occlusion costs 1.9 million neurons

sections.title: Aspek Gizi dalam Stroke

content.text: NUTRITIONAL MANAGEMENT: Dysphagia screening is mandatory before any oral intake. If unsafe swallow: NGT feeding within 24-48 hours. Target 25-30 kcal/kg/day and 1-1.5 g protein/kg/day. Monitor for aspiration. PREVENTION: DASH diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) - rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat dairy, lean protein; low in sodium, saturated fat, added sugars. Mediterranean diet also shows protective effect. Key nutrients: potassium, magnesium, omega-3 fatty acids, folate. Weight management: BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2. Limit sodium to <2.3 g/day (ideally <1.5 g/day for hypertensives).
